rv.q: Without effacing memories of Edward Fox in the role, Atkinson suggests a man whose very niceness is inherently tragic.
How strange to see an actor associated with febrile goofiness being so effective as a blank.
Instead it ventures into Chekhov territory, savouring the complexities of the characters’ tangled pasts.

cn.t: Critics largely praise Rowan Atkinson's restrained, surprisingly effective dramatic turn in this solid revival of Simon Gray's 1981 ensemble comedy about loneliness and detachment, though the production is seen as respectful rather than revelatory.
